items.title: Smooth finite-region Maxwell action, compact variations and the fixed-endpoint particle functional
items.statement:
For the field sector (a)-(b), assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, [[def-countable-choice]]) exactly as inherited from [[lem-em-compact-field-variation]], whose functional and finiteness statement this item instantiates; the definition uses no further choice. The finite-interval Riemann particle sector (c) uses the choice-free curve lemma and does not require that field-sector measure convention. Let the laboratory region, its inertial chart, the field and source objects and the units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-si-conventions]], [[def-em-sources]] and [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]], with $c>0$, $\mu_0>0$ and $\varepsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$, and let worldlines be those of [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]].

(a) [Field action] Let $U\subseteq x(	ext{laboratory region})=cI	imes\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ be a nonempty bounded open set whose closure is a compact subset of that chart image (chart coordinates $x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, $x^0=ct$; [[def-em-lab-geometry]]), let $N\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ be an open neighbourhood of $\overline U$, and let $A:N	o\mathbb R^4$, $x\mapsto(A^0,A^1,A^2,A^3)$, and $j:N	o\mathbb R^4$ be smooth ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]); $A$ is a four-potential in the sense of clause (c) of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] and $j=(cho,J)$ is the four-current of [[def-em-sources]]. Write $A_
u:=\eta_{
u\mu}A^\mu$, $F_{\mu
u}:=\partial_\mu A_
u-\partial_
u A_\mu$, $F^{\mu
u}:=\eta^{\mu\alpha}\eta^{
u eta}F_{\alpha eta}$ and $j^
u A_
u$ for the indicated contraction, with the component dictionary $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ fixed in clause (a) of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] and $\partial_\mu$ the coordinate partial derivatives of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]. Define the **field action** by
$$S[A]:=c^{-1}\int_U\Bigl[- rac{1}{4\mu_0}F_{\mu
u}F^{\mu
u}+j^
u A_
u\Bigr]d\lambda,$$
$d\lambda$ the four-dimensional Lebesgue measure in the chart coordinates ([[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]). Then $S[A]$ is a finite real number, in units of $\mathrm{J\,s}$: the density $-(4\mu_0)^{-1}F_{\mu
u}F^{\mu
u}+j^
u A_
u$ carries $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, $d\lambda$ carries $\mathrm{m^4}$ and $c^{-1}$ carries $\mathrm{s\,m^{-1}}$ ([[def-em-si-conventions]]). With $\kappa:=\mu_0$, $J:=j$ and the same bounded open $U$, one has $S[A]=c^{-1}S_{m math}[A]$, where $S_{m math}$ is the real functional of [[lem-em-compact-field-variation]]; since $c^{-1}>0$, the first variation and the stationarity of $S$ at $A$ are exactly those recorded there.

(b) [Admissible field variations] The field variations are the $h\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R^4)$ ([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]), extended by zero to $N$; for every real $s$ the field $A+sh$ is smooth on $N$, and $s\mapsto S[A+sh]$ is the quadratic polynomial of clause (a) of [[lem-em-compact-field-variation]] with both coefficients multiplied by $c^{-1}$. The field $A$ is **stationary** for $S$ if $ rac{d}{ds} ig|_{s=0}S[A+sh]=0$ for every such $h$.

(c) [Particle functional] Let $m>0$ and $q\in\mathbb R$ ([[def-em-sources]] (a)), let $[a,b]$ be a nondegenerate compact interval, let $X:[a,b]	o A$ be a $C^2$ future timelike massive worldline ([[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]] (a)), and let $A_\mu$ be a $C^2$ covector field on a neighbourhood of the image of $X$. The **particle functional** is the one of [[lem-em-particle-curve-variation]],
$$S_{m pt}[X]:=-mc\int_a^b\sqrt{-\eta(\dot X,\dot X)}\,ds+q\int_a^bA_\mu(X)\dot X^\mu\,ds,$$
with admissible variations the fixed-endpoint $C^2$ variations $h:[a,b]	o V$, $h(a)=h(b)=0$, of that lemma; $m$ is the external rest-mass parameter and $q$ the charge parameter of the framework, and $S_{m pt}$ is a finite real number on the declared class.

(d) [Scope] This item defines only the two functionals, their variation classes and the stationarity predicate; it asserts no stationarity of any configuration, no existence or uniqueness of stationary fields or curves, no boundary conditions, no convergence statement for unbounded regions, no coupled particle-field action and no dynamics of singular sources. Smooth $A$ and $j$ on a neighbourhood of $\overline U$ are required, and point or sheet sources are excluded ([[def-em-sources]] (b)). The physical adoption of stationarity is the postulate recorded later on this page (post-em-stationary-action-model).
items.strategy:
A definition assembled from earlier items, with well-definedness discharged by the cited suppliers. (i) Objects: the region, chart, indices and partial derivatives are those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]; the component conventions $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, $F_{\mu
u}=\partial_\mu A_
u-\partial_
u A_\mu$ and the potential and current dictionary are exactly clauses (a), (c), (d) of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]]; $j=(cho,J)$ and the charge parameter are those of [[def-em-sources]]. (ii) Finiteness: the density is smooth on the open neighbourhood $N$ and $\overline U$ is a compact subset of $N$, hence the density is bounded on $\overline U$; the bounded open $U$ has finite Lebesgue measure, so the integral is absolutely finite, and the stated physical units follow from the quantity table of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. (iii) The functional is literally $c^{-1}$ times the mathematical functional $S$ of [[lem-em-compact-field-variation]] at $\kappa=\mu_0$ and $J=j$ on the same class of smooth fields and compactly supported variations; the lemma's statement (with its Countable Choice hypothesis) supplies the finiteness and the quadratic expansion used in (b), and multiplication by the positive constant $c^{-1}$ preserves first variations and stationarity. (iv) The particle integrals are finite-interval Riemann integrals, and that sector uses no Countable Choice. The particle functional is the exact functional of [[lem-em-particle-curve-variation]], cited rather than redefined; the identification of its curves with the framework's massive worldlines is clause (a) of [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]]. (v) Scope: no choice beyond the inherited hypothesis, no existence, no boundary data, no singular sources, no coupled action.
items.physical_scope: Definition of two real functionals of the smooth finite-region model: the field action on a bounded chart region with a smooth prescribed four-current and compactly supported smooth field variations, and the fixed-endpoint particle functional on $C^2$ future timelike massive worldlines with a prescribed $C^2$ external four-potential. Excluded: existence or minimality of stationary configurations, boundary conditions, unbounded regions, singular sources, and any coupled particle-field action.

items.title: Adopt stationary Maxwell action as alternative physical formulation
items.statement:
The model adopts the following formulation principle as an alternative to postulating the field equations and the force law directly. (i) [Field sector] A smooth field $A:N\to\mathbb R^4$ on the region $U$ of clause (a) of [[def-em-field-action-definition]] is dynamically admissible exactly when it is stationary for the field action $S[A]$ under all compactly supported smooth variations $h\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R^4)$ in the sense of clause (b) of that definition: $\frac{d}{ds}\big|_{s=0}S[A+sh]=0$ for every such $h$. (ii) [Particle sector] For a prescribed external four-potential $A_\mu$ on a neighbourhood of the image of a $C^2$ future timelike massive worldline $X$, the motion is dynamically admissible exactly when $X$ is stationary for the particle functional $S_{\rm pt}$ of clause (c) of that definition under all fixed-endpoint $C^2$ variations.

This is an adopted assumption of the model, not a theorem, not a derivation from the remaining postulates and not an empirical result. It asserts stationarity only: it does not assert that a stationary configuration is a local or global minimum, that stationary configurations exist or are unique, that the action functional is uniquely determined or forced by symmetry, that no other action formulation is possible, or that the two sectors can be coupled into a single well-posed action for singular sources. No Noether theorem, no symmetry-to-conservation machinery and no matter dynamics beyond the prescribed potential are assumed. The conditional deductions of this pair are: on the declared smooth classes, (i) is equivalent to the inhomogeneous tensor field equation $\partial_\mu F^{\mu\nu}=-\mu_0j^\nu$ and, for potential-represented fields, to the smooth-branch Maxwell equations, and (ii) is equivalent to the framework's adopted four-force equation $m\,dU/d\tau=q\,\Phi(U)$; both deductions are recorded separately on this page, and this postulate asserts neither.
items.strategy: An explicit adopted-assumption contract, formulated by reference to the precise functionals, variation classes and stationarity predicate of [[def-em-field-action-definition]]. The non-derivation is deliberate: the postulate adopts a variational formulation of the same field and particle dynamics as an alternative model principle, and the conditional Euler-Lagrange calculations about the adopted functionals (the compact-variation field computation and the fixed-endpoint curve computation) are theorems recorded separately, not proofs of the postulate. The scope sentences exclude minimality, existence, uniqueness, symmetry-forcing, coupling and Noether content. The physical source context is the action-principle presentation of classical electrodynamics in the cited treatments, which likewise present stationarity as an adopted principle and do not prove it; the source row recording that the interaction form is not fixed by general considerations alone supports exactly this non-derivation scope. No choice principle is used by this item; its single formulation prerequisite carries the hypotheses noted there.
items.physical_scope: Adopted formulation principle: stationarity of the precisely defined smooth finite-region field action and of the fixed-endpoint particle functional under the declared variations, as an alternative presentation of the field equations and the force law. Not asserted: minimality, existence, uniqueness, symmetry-forcing, uniqueness of the action, coupling of the sectors, or any empirical claim.

items.title: Compact gauge variation is boundary-free for conserved source
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, [[def-countable-choice]]), inherited through the componentwise fundamental-variation step of [[lem-em-fundamental-variation-lemma]] and through [[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]]. Let $U,N,A,j,F,S$ and the constants $c,\mu_0,\varepsilon_0$ be as in clauses (a)-(b) of [[def-em-field-action-definition]]: $U$ bounded open with $\overline U$ compact in the laboratory chart image $cI	imes\Omega$, $N$ an open neighbourhood of $\overline U$, $A$ and $j$ smooth on $N$, $F_{\mu
u}=\partial_\mu A_
u-\partial_
u A_\mu$, $j=(cho,J)$ with the source fields of [[def-em-sources]], and $S[A]=c^{-1}\int_U igl[-(4\mu_0)^{-1}F_{\mu
u}F^{\mu
u}+j^
u A_
u igr]d\lambda$. For $\chi\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R)$ write $\partial^\sharp\chi$ for the vector field with contravariant components $(\partial^\sharp\chi)^\mu:=\partial^\mu\chi=\eta^{\mu
u}\partial_
u\chi$ ([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]). It is a compactly supported smooth field variation. Thus $A^\mu\mapsto A^\mu+\partial^\mu\chi$ lowers to $A_
u\mapsto A_
u+\partial_
u\chi$; $A+\partial^\sharp\chi$ denotes this vector addition.

(a) [Exact gauge difference, no boundary term] For every such $\chi$ one has $F_{\mu
u}(A+\partial^\sharp\chi)=F_{\mu
u}(A)$ on $U$, because $\partial_\mu\partial_
u\chi-\partial_
u\partial_\mu\chi=0$ for the smooth $\chi$ ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]); consequently the field term of $S$ is unchanged and
$$S[A+\partial^\sharp\chi]-S[A]=c^{-1}\int_Uj^\mu\,\partial_\mu\chi\,d\lambda=-c^{-1}\int_U(\partial_\mu j^\mu)\,\chi\,d\lambda,$$
the second equality being the distributional integration-by-parts identity for the locally integrable fields $j^\mu$ and the smooth compactly supported $\chi$ ([[def-distributional-derivative]], [[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]]); no boundary term arises precisely because $\chi$ is compactly supported in $U$.

(b) [Equivalence for smooth sources] If $\partial_\mu j^\mu=0$ on $U$ (the source is conserved), then $S[A+\partial^\sharp\chi]=S[A]$ for every $\chi\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R)$. Conversely, if $S[A+\partial^\sharp\chi]=S[A]$ for every such $\chi$, then $\partial_\mu j^\mu=0$ pointwise on $U$: the function $\partial_\mu j^\mu$ is continuous on the open $U$ and pairs to zero against every compactly supported smooth $\chi$, so [[lem-em-fundamental-variation-lemma]] applies. Hence for smooth prescribed sources the invariance of the field action under all compact gauge variations is equivalent to the conservation of the four-current.

(c) [Maxwell-compatible sources] Suppose in addition that the field pair $(E,B)$ represented by $A$ through the potential dictionary of clause (c) of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] and the source fields $(ho,J)$ satisfy the smooth branch of the vacuum Maxwell equations on $U$ (equivalently, by clause (a) of [[pthm-em-tensor-maxwell-equivalence]], the tensor system $\partial_\mu F^{\mu
u}=-\mu_0j^
u$ together with the cyclic identity). Then clause (a) of [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]] gives $\partial_tho+\operatorname{div}J=0$ on $U$ ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]), which in the chart reads $\partial_\mu j^\mu=\partial_0(cho)+\operatorname{div}J=c^{-1}\partial_t(cho)+\operatorname{div}J=0$; hence $S[A+\partial^\sharp\chi]=S[A]$ for every compact gauge variation.

(d) [Distributional reading] If $j^\mu$ is a distribution on $U$ ([[def-distributional-derivative]]), the gauge-difference pairing $c^{-1}\langle j^\mu,\partial_\mu\chiangle$ is defined for every test function $\chi\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R)$ and equals $-c^{-1}\langle\partial_\mu j^\mu,\chiangle$ by the signed definition of the distributional derivative; hence the pairing vanishes for every compact gauge variation if and only if $\partial_\mu j^\mu=0$ as a distribution. This is a statement about the pairing only: the smooth $j$ of the definition is retained whenever the functional $S$ itself is used, and no products of distributions are formed.

Scope: the item computes the gauge variation of the field action and its compatibility with source conservation; it does not derive the field equations from gauge invariance, does not assert that conservation of a source implies stationarity, does not treat global or topological obstructions, and uses no Noether machinery.
items.strategy:
Direct finite computation plus the fundamental lemma. (a) Since $A^\mu$ is contravariant, the gauge variation is $\partial^\mu\chi$; lowering gives $\eta_{
u\mu}\eta^{\mu\alpha}\partial_\alpha\chi=\partial_
u\chi$. Since $A$ and $\chi$ are smooth, $F_{\mu
u}(A+\partial^\sharp\chi)=F_{\mu
u}(A)+\partial_\mu\partial_
u\chi-\partial_
u\partial_\mu\chi=F_{\mu
u}(A)$ by [[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]; the quadratic field term is therefore constant along the gauge path, and only the source term changes: $S[A+\partial^\sharp\chi]-S[A]=c^{-1}\int_Uj^\mu\partial_\mu\chi\,d\lambda$, using the linearity of the Lebesgue integral for the finite integrable functions ([[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]], [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). Treat each $j^\mu$ as its regular distribution ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]]); the definition of the distributional derivative gives $\langle j^\mu,\partial_\mu\chiangle=-\langle\partial_\mu j^\mu,\chiangle$, and for the $C^1$ field $j^\mu$ the distributional derivative equals the classical one ([[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]]), which yields the displayed second equality. Because $\chi$ is compactly supported in the open $U$ there is no boundary term. (b) If $\partial_\mu j^\mu=0$ identically, (a) gives invariance. Conversely $\partial_\mu j^\mu$ is continuous on $U$, and the vanishing of its integral against every compactly supported smooth $\chi$ forces it to vanish pointwise by [[lem-em-fundamental-variation-lemma]]. (c) Under the smooth Maxwell branch, clause (a) of [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]] gives the continuity equation; the chart identity $\partial_\mu j^\mu=c^{-1}\partial_t(cho)+\operatorname{div}J=\partial_tho+\operatorname{div}J$ is the component computation of [[def-em-sources]] (c) and [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], so (b) applies. (d) For a distributional $j^\mu$ the pairing identity is the definition of the distributional derivative, and the vanishing criterion is the definition of the zero distribution. The Countable Choice assumption enters exactly through the two cited conversions (the pointwise localization against all smooth tests and the classical-compatibility of the distributional derivative); no other choice principle is used.
items.physical_scope: Conditional statement about the smooth finite-region action: for a smooth prescribed four-current on a bounded chart region, the exact gauge difference of the field action under compactly supported smooth gauge parameters, and the equivalence between invariance under all compact gauges and conservation of the four-current, including the Maxwell-compatible instantiation through charge continuity and the distributional reading of the pairing. Excluded: derivation of the field equations from gauge invariance, stationarity conclusions, global or topological obstructions, Noether machinery, and rough-source products.

items.title: Action stationarity implies the inhomogeneous Maxwell equations
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, [[def-countable-choice]]), inherited from [[lem-em-compact-field-variation]]. Let $U\subseteq cI	imes\Omega$, $N$, the smooth fields $A,j$ on $N$, the components $A_
u$, $F_{\mu
u}=\partial_\mu A_
u-\partial_
u A_\mu$, $F^{\mu
u}$, the source convention $j=(cho,J)$, the constants $c,\mu_0,\varepsilon_0$ and the field action $S[A]=c^{-1}\int_U igl[-(4\mu_0)^{-1}F_{\mu
u}F^{\mu
u}+j^
u A_
u igr]d\lambda$ be as in clauses (a)-(b) of [[def-em-field-action-definition]] with the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]].

Then the following are equivalent: (i) $A$ is stationary for $S$ under all $h\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R^4)$, i.e. the adopted field equation of [[post-em-stationary-action-model]] (i); (ii) $\partial_\mu F^{\mu
u}=-\mu_0j^
u$ at every point of $U$ for every $
u\in\{0,1,2,3\}$.

Consequently, if $A$ is stationary then: (a) [Inhomogeneous tensor equations] $\partial_\mu F^{\mu
u}=-\mu_0 j^
u$ on $U$; (b) [Homogeneous tensor equations] $\partial_\lambda F_{\mu
u}+\partial_\mu F_{
u\lambda}+\partial_
u F_{\lambda\mu}=0$ on $U$, since $A$ is smooth and its mixed partial derivatives commute; (c) [Laboratory Maxwell equations] define $\varphi:=-cA_0$, the spatial potential vector $\mathbf A:=(A_1,A_2,A_3)$, $E:=-
abla\varphi-\partial_t\mathbf A$ and $B:=\operatorname{curl}\mathbf A$ by clause (c) of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]], and $(ho,J)$ by $j=(cho,J)$ ([[def-em-sources]]); then on $U$ the four smooth-branch Maxwell equations hold, equivalently the eight scalar equations (TM1)-(TM2) of [[pthm-em-tensor-maxwell-equivalence]] hold with these fields and sources, i.e. $\operatorname{div}E=ho/\varepsilon_0$, $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ and $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$.

The statement concerns a given smooth pair $(A,j)$ on the declared region: it asserts no existence of a stationary field, imposes no boundary or decay condition, and excludes the weak, distributional, singular-support and non-potential-represented branches. The equivalence is conditional on the adopted stationary-action postulate and makes no empirical claim.
items.strategy:
Instantiate the compact-variation lemma at $\kappa=\mu_0$ and $J=j$, then translate through the component equivalence. Since $S[A]=c^{-1}S_{m math}[A]$ with $c^{-1}>0$ and $S_{m math}$ the functional of [[lem-em-compact-field-variation]] on the same region and field class, the derivative of $s\mapsto S[A+sh]$ vanishes for every $h$ exactly when that of $s\mapsto S_{m math}[A+sh]$ does; by clause (c) of that lemma this is equivalent to $\partial_\mu F^{\mu
u}=-\mu_0j^
u$ for all $
u$ at every point of $U$. This proves (i)$\Leftrightarrow$(ii). Clause (b) is the closedness of the exact two-form: for smooth $A$ the cyclic sum $\partial_\lambda F_{\mu
u}+\partial_\mu F_{
u\lambda}+\partial_
u F_{\lambda\mu}$ is a sum of six second partial derivatives of $A$ grouped in cancelling pairs by [[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]. Clause (c): the potential dictionary of clause (c) of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] identifies the components of $F$ defined here with those of the electromagnetic two-form built from $\varphi$ and $\mathbf A$; with clause (a) of that definition and $j=(cho,J)$, clauses (a) and (b) are exactly the systems (TM1) and (TM2), so clause (a) of [[pthm-em-tensor-maxwell-equivalence]] - the component equivalence on the smooth branch, applied to these $C^\infty$ objects with the stated regularity - converts them into the four displayed equations and back. All derivatives are classical derivatives of smooth functions; the compact-support integration by parts is the supplied classical/weak-derivative compatibility calculation; no boundary term or rough-field weak-model claim is introduced, and the only choice assumption is the inherited one noted in the statement.
items.physical_scope: Conditional statement about a smooth four-potential and smooth prescribed four-current on a bounded chart region: stationarity of the adopted field action under all compactly supported smooth variations is equivalent to the inhomogeneous tensor equation, and stationarity implies the full smooth-branch Maxwell equations for the represented field pair and source. Excluded: existence of stationary fields, boundary and decay conditions, weak and distributional branches, singular sources, non-potential-represented fields, and any empirical claim.

items.title: Relativistic prescribed-field particle action yields the Lorentz force
items.statement:
The finite-interval Riemann particle-sector calculation is choice-free: the field-sector Countable Choice convention of [[def-em-field-action-definition]] is not used here. Let worldlines, four-velocities and proper times be those of [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]], let $F$ be the electromagnetic two-form with the component and potential dictionary of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]], and let $m>0$ and $q\in\mathbb R$ be the framework's external rest-mass and charge parameters ([[def-em-sources]] (a)). Let $[a,b]$ be a nondegenerate compact interval, let $X:[a,b]\to A$ be a $C^2$ future timelike massive worldline (clause (a) of [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]]), let $A_\mu$ be a $C^2$ covector field - the prescribed external four-potential - on a neighbourhood of the image of $X$, and let $S_{\rm pt}$ be the particle functional of clause (c) of [[def-em-field-action-definition]], i.e. the functional $-mc\int_a^b\sqrt{-\eta(\dot X,\dot X)}\,ds+q\int_a^bA_\mu(X)\dot X^\mu\,ds$ of [[lem-em-particle-curve-variation]].

Then, under the adopted stationary-action model for the particle sector ([[post-em-stationary-action-model]] (ii)), for every fixed-endpoint $C^2$ variation $h$ with $h(a)=h(b)=0$ the curve $X+\varepsilon h$ is future timelike for all sufficiently small $|\varepsilon|$, and the following are equivalent: (i) $X$ is stationary for $S_{\rm pt}$ under all such variations; (ii) $m\,dU_\nu/d\tau=qF_{\nu\mu}U^\mu$ on $[a,b]$, where $F=dA$ and $\tau$ is the proper time of $X$; (iii) the four-force equation $m\,dU/d\tau=q\,\Phi(U)$ of the framework's adopted covariant coupling [[pthm-em-relativistic-lorentz-force]], where $\Phi$ is the raised-index field operator $\eta(\Phi(u),w)=F(w,u)$. In particular the stationary-action formulation of the particle sector is equivalent, for prescribed external potentials, to the adopted Lorentz coupling; the coordinate equations $\frac{dp}{dt}=q(E+v\times B)$ and $\frac{d(\gamma mc^2)}{dt}=qE\cdot v$ of [[pthm-em-relativistic-lorentz-force]] then hold wherever the laboratory reading is $C^2$.

Scope: the potential, hence the field, is prescribed and external to the particle; the particle's own field, radiation reaction and self-force are excluded, as are magnetic monopoles, zero or variable mass, coupled particle-field existence and any approximation of the trajectory over a time interval. The equivalence is conditional on the adopted postulates and makes no empirical claim.
items.physical_scope: Conditional statement about one massive charged particle on a future timelike $C^2$ worldline in a prescribed external $C^2$ four-potential: the fixed-endpoint stationarity of the particle functional is equivalent to the covariant four-force equation and to the adopted Lorentz coupling, with the coordinate force and power laws following. Excluded: self-field, radiation reaction, self-force, monopoles, zero or variable mass, coupled particle-field existence, trajectory approximation, and any empirical claim.

items.title: Stationary functional need not be a minimum
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, inherited from the field-action measure suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]]); no additional choice is used. Work in [[def-em-field-action-definition]] with the coordinate box $U=(-1,1)^4$ lying compactly inside the chosen laboratory chart, constants $c,\mu_0>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ ([[def-em-si-conventions]]) and $j=0$.

(a) [Coordinate and physical forms] With $x^0=ct$, set $U_t:=\{(t,x):(ct,x)\in U\}=(-1/c,1/c)\times(-1,1)^3$. The exact field dictionary gives
$$S[A]=\frac{1}{2c\mu_0}\int_U(|E|^2/c^2-|B|^2)d\lambda=\frac12\int_{U_t}(\varepsilon_0|E|^2-|B|^2/\mu_0)dt\,d^3x.$$
Also $S[\lambda A]=\lambda^2S[A]$ for every real $\lambda$.

(b) [Stationarity] $A=0$ is stationary: the actual first-variation coefficient of [[lem-em-compact-field-variation]] is $-\mu_0^{-1}F^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu h_\nu+j^\nu h_\nu$, and the action variation is $c^{-1}$ times its integral. Both terms vanish at $F=0,j=0$.

(c) [Positive direction] Choose $\theta\in C_c^\infty(U)$ with $\nabla_x\theta\not\equiv0$. Set the covariant components $h_0=\theta,h_i=0$, equivalently the contravariant variation $h^0=-\theta,h^i=0$. Then $E=c\nabla_x\theta$, $B=0$, and
$$S[h]=\frac{1}{2c\mu_0}\int_U|\nabla_x\theta|^2d\lambda>0.$$

(d) [Negative directions with a fixed compact support] Choose nonzero nonnegative smooth bumps $\eta,\varphi,\psi_2,\psi_3\in C_c^\infty((-1/2,1/2))$ using [[lem-test-function-cutoffs-and-euclidean-localization]]. Extend them by zero to $\mathbb R$. For integers $N\ge1$ define the contravariant variation with only its second spatial component nonzero:
$$h^{(N)2}(x)=\eta(x^0)\varphi(Nx^1)\psi_2(x^2)\psi_3(x^3).$$
All supports lie in one fixed compact subset of $U$. Writing $f_N=h^{(N)2}$, its fields are $E=-c(\partial_0f_N)e_2$ and $B=-(\partial_3f_N)e_1+(\partial_1f_N)e_3$. Define finite constants, with all one-dimensional integrals over $(-1,1)$,
$$C_E=(\int\eta'^2)(\int\varphi^2)(\int\psi_2^2)(\int\psi_3^2),\quad C_B=(\int\eta^2)(\int\varphi'^2)(\int\psi_2^2)(\int\psi_3^2)>0,$$
$$C_3=(\int\eta^2)(\int\varphi^2)(\int\psi_2^2)(\int\psi_3'^2)\ge0.$$
Exact substitution and Fubini give
$$\int_U|E|^2/c^2d\lambda=C_E/N,\qquad\int_U|B|^2d\lambda=C_BN+C_3/N,$$
$$S[h^{(N)}]=\frac{1}{2c\mu_0}\left(\frac{C_E-C_3}{N}-C_BN\right)\longrightarrow-\infty.$$
Thus a fixed sufficiently large $N$ supplies one negative direction $h_-$; the direction $h_+$ of (c) is positive. For nonzero $\lambda$, their rescalings keep their respective signs, and each action tends to zero in absolute value as $\lambda\to0$. A single fixed negative direction is not claimed to change sign under rescaling.

(e) [Every usual neighbourhood] Fix those two directions before rescaling. For each derivative multi-index, every compact-set supremum of a derivative of $\lambda h_\pm$ is $|\lambda|$ times the finite supremum for that fixed smooth compactly supported direction. Thus both tend to zero in the usual $C^k$, smooth compact-convergence and fixed-support and LF test-function topologies ([[def-fixed-support-test-function-frechet-space]], [[def-test-function-topology]]) (and in any usual function-space topology with continuous scalar multiplication). Every such neighbourhood of zero therefore contains configurations of positive and negative action, arbitrarily small in magnitude. The stationary zero is neither a local minimum nor a local maximum. This is a computation in the declared smooth finite-region model, not a claim about actual fields or measurements; other sources or boundary/variation restrictions require their own analysis.
items.strategy:
(a) Substitute $\tfrac12F_{\mu\nu}F^{\mu\nu}=|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2$ from [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] into the action. The coordinate change $x^0=ct$ has $d\lambda=c\,dt\,d^3x$ and changes the time interval to $(-1/c,1/c)$, so the physical-time formula uses $U_t$, not the unscaled coordinate box. Linearity of $F$ and the quadratic functional give the scaling law. (b) uses the exact raised-field/lowered-test coefficient and the overall factor $c^{-1}$ of the definition; at zero it vanishes pointwise.

(c) Direct differentiation gives the stated electric-only field. The continuous nonnegative integrand is positive on a small box because the spatial gradient is nonzero somewhere, so its integral is positive under the declared field-sector measure convention.

(d) Derive the three displayed field components by the product/chain rules. Every selected bump is smooth with compact support strictly inside $(-1/2,1/2)$, so all $h^{(N)}$ share an interior compact support. The nonzero compact bump $\varphi$ cannot have $\varphi'\equiv0$: FTC would make it constant on $\mathbb R$, and compact support would then force zero. Thus the continuous square $\varphi'^2$ is positive on an interval and has a positive integral; all undifferentiated bump-square integrals are likewise positive. For $N\ge1$, [[thm-substitution]] with the affine map $y=Nx^1$ gives $\int_{-1}^1\varphi(Nx^1)^2dx^1=N^{-1}\int_{-N}^N\varphi(y)^2dy=N^{-1}\int_{-1}^1\varphi(y)^2dy$, and the same identity for $\varphi'^2$. These are ordinary continuous compactly supported Riemann integrals; [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]] converts them to the action's Lebesgue integrals under the already-declared Countable Choice. [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] factors each smooth compact-support squared product. The time derivative supplies $C_E/N$; the $x^1$ derivative supplies $C_BN$, and the $x^3$ derivative supplies $C_3/N$. No endpoint touching the boundary and no false polynomial lower bound are used. Since $C_B>0$, choose one sufficiently large integer $N$ with negative action. Hold it fixed during rescaling.

(e) Quadratic homogeneity keeps the positive and negative signs separately. On the common fixed compact support, the seminorms $p_m$ of [[def-fixed-support-test-function-frechet-space]] obey $p_m(\lambda h)=|\lambda|p_m(h)$. In the LF definition [[def-test-function-topology]], every seminorm similarly obeys $q(\lambda h)=|\lambda|q(h)$, and a zero neighbourhood contains finitely many such bounds, so the line also tends to zero there. Scaling each fixed compact direction makes every derivative seminorm tend to zero and makes its action magnitude tend to zero. Hence every stated usual neighbourhood contains both signs, proving the full non-extremum claim without a claim that scaling a negative direction creates a positive one. This local functional counterexample is not a source's numbered physical result or an empirical assertion.
items.physical_scope: Worked computation in the smooth finite-region field action with the box region and no source: the stationary configuration of the adopted model is a saddle of the indefinite quadratic functional, with explicit compact variations of both signs and arbitrarily small magnitude. Excluded: any claim about physical fields or measurements, minimality of the adopted action, and applicability beyond the declared region and functional.

items.title: A compact test variation and gauge-source sign check
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, inherited from the cited theorems. Work in the field-action setting of [[def-em-field-action-definition]] with $U=(-1,1)^4$, constants $c,\mu_0>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ ([[def-em-si-conventions]]), and the component dictionary of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]]: $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F^{0i}=E_i/c$, $F^{10}=-E_1/c$.

(a) [Source-free zero field] For $j\equiv0$ and $A=0$ the first-variation coefficient (whose integral is multiplied by $c^{-1}$) $-\mu_0^{-1}F^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu h_\nu+j^\nu h_\nu$ of clause (a) of [[lem-em-compact-field-variation]] vanishes identically for every $h\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R^4)$, because $F(A)=0$ and $j=0$; hence every compact first variation of $S$ at $A=0$ is zero and $A=0$ is stationary.

(b) [A non-trivial compact test variation] Let $A$ be the smooth potential with $A_0(x)=x^1$ and $A_1=A_2=A_3=0$, and let $j\equiv0$. Then $F_{01}=-\partial_1A_0=-1$, $F^{01}=+1$, $F^{10}=-1$ and all other components vanish, so the represented field is $E=(c,0,0)$, $B=0$ (clause (b) of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]]) and $\partial_\mu F^{\mu\nu}=0$ on $U$. By the equivalence of [[pthm-em-action-maxwell-variation]], $A$ is stationary; directly, for every $h\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R^4)$ the first variation of $S$ at $A$ is
$$\frac{d}{ds}\Big|_{s=0}S[A+sh]=-\frac{1}{c\mu_0}\int_U\bigl(\partial_0h_1-\partial_1h_0\bigr)d\lambda=\frac{1}{c\mu_0}\int_U\bigl(\partial_1h_0-\partial_0h_1\bigr)d\lambda=0,$$
where each of $\int_U\partial_0h_1\,d\lambda$ and $\int_U\partial_1h_0\,d\lambda$ vanishes by the fundamental theorem in one variable combined with Fubini, and no boundary term appears because $h$ is compactly supported in $U$ ([[thm-newton-leibniz-with-interior-derivative]], [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]], [[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]).

(c) [Gauge-source sign check with actual overlap] Independently choose the smooth prescribed source $j^0=c\rho(x^0)$, $j^i=0$, with nonzero nonnegative $\rho\in C_c^\infty((-1/4,1/4))$ extended by zero. Choose $0\le\zeta\in C_c^\infty((-1,1))$ with $\zeta=1$ near $[-1/2,1/2]$, and nonzero nonnegative $\psi\in C_c^\infty((-1,1)^3)$, supplied by [[lem-test-function-cutoffs-and-euclidean-localization]]. Put $\varphi_\pm(u)=(2\pm u)\zeta(u)$ and $\chi_\pm(x)=\varphi_\pm(x^0)\psi(x^1,x^2,x^3)$. Both $\varphi_\pm$ are nonnegative compact bumps, but they are not globally monotone: on the entire support of $\rho$ their derivatives equal $+1$ and $-1$, respectively. Use the contravariant gauge variations $(\partial^\sharp\chi_\pm)^\mu=\eta^{\mu\nu}\partial_\nu\chi_\pm$ from [[pthm-em-action-gauge-source-compatibility]]. Then
$$S[A+\partial^\sharp\chi_\pm]-S[A]=\left(\int_{-1}^1\rho\varphi_\pm'\,dx^0\right)\left(\int_{(-1,1)^3}\psi\,d^3x\right)=\pm\left(\int\rho\right)\left(\int\psi\right),$$
which is strictly positive for $+$ and strictly negative for $-$, since both factors are positive. Integration by parts gives exactly the same value as $-c^{-1}\int_U(\partial_\mu j^\mu)\chi_\pm d\lambda$ with $\partial_\mu j^\mu=c\rho'$. This verifies the relative sign of the $+j^\mu A_\mu$ coupling, the raised-vector/covariant-lowered gauge shift and the conservation condition, using explicitly overlapping supports. If instead $\rho$ is constant on the whole neighbourhood, the source is conserved and every compact gauge difference is zero. No compact nonzero globally increasing or decreasing function is used.

(d) [Scope] The example is an exact computation in the declared smooth finite-region model; it asserts no existence of sources or fields, no numerical value of $\mu_0$, and no global gauge statement.
items.strategy: Direct substitution in the declared functionals. (a) is the first-variation formula of [[lem-em-compact-field-variation]] with $F=0$ and $j=0$; the pointwise vanishing of the integrand gives a vanishing integral for every $h$. (b) The components follow from clause (a) of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]]: $F_{01}=\partial_0A_1-\partial_1A_0=-1$, $F^{01}=\eta^{00}\eta^{11}F_{01}=+1$, $F^{10}=-1$. The coefficient equation $\partial_\mu F^{\mu\nu}=-\mu_0j^\nu$ holds because $F$ is constant and $j=0$, so [[pthm-em-action-maxwell-variation]] gives stationarity. The direct computation uses the first-variation expression of the cited lemma and the one-variable fundamental theorem for the compactly supported functions $h_0,h_1$, with Fubini reducing the four-dimensional integral; the absence of boundary terms is exactly the compact-support hypothesis. (c) Apply the corrected raised-gradient gauge formula. The cutoff $\zeta$ is one on a neighbourhood of the support of $\rho$, so $\zeta'=0$ there and $\varphi_+'=1$, $\varphi_-'=-1$ there. Although both compact functions must turn back to zero outside that plateau, those derivative changes do not meet $\rho$. Thus Fubini gives the two signed products of positive integrals exactly. The signs agree with one-dimensional [[thm-integration-by-parts]], whose endpoint term is zero because the factors are compactly supported. Constant $\rho$ instead gives $\int\rho\varphi_\pm'=0$ by FTC, consistently with source conservation. The prescribed source and potential here need not satisfy Maxwell together; this is the deliberately nonconserved-source functional witness, not a claim of a dynamically admissible source-field configuration. All relevant functions are smooth; the existing field-sector Countable Choice convention is retained.
items.physical_scope: Worked computation in the smooth finite-region field action on a box: the explicit first variation of a constant-field potential vanishes with no boundary term, and the exact gauge difference of the action pins the relative sign between the source coupling, the gauge shift and source conservation, including a non-conserved source exhibiting both signs. Excluded: existence statements, numerical values of constants, and any global or empirical claim.
